learning_outcomes.text: Know the principles of computer operation; the principles of object-oriented programming; computational approaches to problem solving (algorithms) and data structure design.
Develop the necessary competencies for simple application development in Java.
Know the principles of computer operation and object-oriented programming; understand elementary approaches to problem solving (algorithms) and data structure design.
Develop the necessary competencies for simple application development in Java.
Know the principles of computer operation; the principles of object-oriented programming; computational approaches to problem solving (algorithms) and data structure design.
Develop the necessary competencies for simple application development in Java.

Knowledge and understanding: At the end of the course, students will know the principles of computer operation and object-oriented programming; elementary approaches to problem solving (algorithms) and data structure design. They will also acquire the necessary competencies for developing simple applications in Java.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: Students will be able to analyze a problem and design its solution by coding it with an algorithm and implementing it in a program using the Java programming language.
Autonomy of judgment: Students will develop the ability to evaluate the quality of algorithmic solutions based on complexity criteria.
Communication skills: Ability to write clear and understandable code.
Learning ability: Acquisition of the ability of abstraction and problem solving.

syllabus_topics: COMPUTER ORGANIZATION
Central processing unit, central memory, mass storage devices, input and output devices
Information representation, numbering systems and conversions
FUNDAMENTAL CONCEPTS OF PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES
Types of programming languages
Program execution via compilation and interpretation

ALGORITHMS AND COMPUTATIONAL COMPLEXITY

RECURSION

teaching_methods: Use of didactic technologies (Moodle and/or other didactic tools, software, videos, quizzes, Wooclap)

assessment_methods.method: Knowledge assessment via quizzes (multiple-choice or short-answer questions)

assessment_rules: The evaluation will be based on the understanding of the topics covered and the ability to apply them autonomously in the development of simple Java applications. The exam consists of two parts: a theory test and a programming test. Formative assessment includes peer evaluation and comparison with junior tutors for some sections, and self-assessment quizzes and Wooclap for others. For sections B and D, the use of generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT or Lucrez-IA) is not permitted during exercises and exams. For section C, generative AI is permitted as support for individual preparation, but students are responsible for verifying generated information. For section A, generative AI is not permitted during exercises and exams.
